\begin{theorem}[All-output affine section]\label{thm:section}
Under these checked hypotheses, a Las Vegas algorithm with expected
polynomial bit complexity manufactures an invertible $h_*\in h_0+W$.
It constructs $v_*$ with $\iota(v_*)=h_*-h_0$ and the affine map
\[
 \sigma(y)=x_{\rm aff}+J(h_*^{-1}y,v_*)
\]
satisfying the original marked-gate identity
\[
 Q(\sigma(y))=c_0+P_Oy\quad\text{for every }y\in O.
\]
The map $\sigma$ is injective. Its image is an affine input subspace of
dimension $\dim_2O$ containing one representative of every consistent
marked target. No target orbit, common-carrier, nested/crossing phase,
or bounded-codimension hypothesis is required.

A native complete-register equality therefore has a witness exactly when
its reversed target satisfies the acquired output dependencies. The same
compiled section is reusable for every target. It is not a uniform sampler
of the full original-input fiber.
\end{theorem}

\section{Invertible completion of every affine partial trace}

Set $T_0=D_0h_0$. A candidate $h=D_0^{-1}T$ lies in $h_0+W$ exactly when
\[
 \tau(B(T-T_0))=0\qquad\text{for all }B\in A.
\]
Partition component $i$ into $h_i\times h_i$ blocks of size $s_i$.
Nondegeneracy of the matrix trace and field trace pairings makes the
conditions precisely
\begin{equation}\label{eq:partial}
 \sum_{\alpha=1}^{h_i}T_{i,\alpha\alpha}
 =H_i:=\sum_{\alpha=1}^{h_i}(T_0)_{i,\alpha\alpha}\quad(1\le i\le b).
\end{equation}
All off-component blocks are unrestricted. The unknown nonzero trace
factor $\gamma$ cannot change these equivalences because the whole
$F$-linear factor $M_{s_i}(F)$ is tested.

For component $i$, put $H_i$ in block $(1,1)$, identities in blocks
$(\alpha,\alpha+1)$ for $1\le\alpha<h_i$ and $(h_i,1)$, and zero elsewhere.
For $h_i=2$ this gives
\[
 T_i=\begin{pmatrix}H_i&I\\I&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its diagonal-block sum is $H_i$. It is invertible for every $H_i$: the
last equation in $T_i z=0$ forces $z_1=0$, the middle equations force
$z_3,\ldots,z_{h_i}=0$, and the first forces $z_2=0$.
Thus $T=\bigoplus_iT_i$ is invertible and satisfies \eqref{eq:partial}.
The map $h_*=D_0^{-1}T$ is invertible and lies in the exact affine slice.
The code independently verifies actual Hom-space membership, every
annihilator equation, invertibility, and the unique actual-right-input
coordinates.

## C. Constructing one invertible affine representative

For a regular dual D=A D0 with actual common scalar operators, zero common
kernel and equal source/target dimension, choose field bases in primitive
left ideals and transport them by connecting matrix units. Their images lie
in orthogonal primitive summands. The resulting sum D0 is injective by the
common-kernel condition, hence invertible by equal dimensions; the regular
dimension identity gives A D0=D. Equal field degrees alone are insufficient.

Under multiplicity h_i>=2, each affine partial-trace condition can be met by
an invertible block companion matrix: for h=2 use [[H,I],[I,0]], and for
higher h use the forward cycle with H on its first diagonal. Thus one fixed
h* lies in h0+W and is invertible. The original affine section
sigma(y)=x_aff+J(h*^-1 y,v*) works for every consistent marked output.
It is a search operation, independent of c, target-carrier arrangement and
one-copy target restrictions. It is not the full-fiber counting or uniform
sampling operation. A coefficient-by-coefficient quadratic composition
certificate is stronger than a few target probes. Multiplicity one can
defeat this invertible-transversal construction; that is not preimage-search
hardness or a claim that all other sections fail.
